title: Student Syndicate
transcript:
Speaker 0: Section three. You will hear three geology students, Andy, Bob, and Helen, talking about forming a study syndicate for their forthcoming examinations. First, you have some time to look at questions 21 to 25 on page six. Now listen carefully and answer questions 21 to 25.
Speaker 1: Right then. Are we ready?
Bob, Helen?
Speaker 1: Yeah. And is someone taking notes for John? He's at a tutorial, isn't he?
Speaker 2: Yeah. I'll let him know what we agree.
Speaker 1: Good. Okay. Well, first thing is, has anyone apart from me actually been in a study syndicate before? No.
Speaker 3: What does it actually involve, Andy?
Speaker 1: Well, the idea is that it's a way for us for students to study together without a teacher.
Speaker 2: Oh, yeah. Right. When
Speaker 1: I did it last time, I found it helpful because, well, as I said, there's no teacher, so it means we're teaching one another. And I found I I really learned a lot through having to teach it myself. It seemed a very good way to learn.
Speaker 3: And presumably, it gives us the chance to share ideas as well.
Speaker 2: And you get fuller notes if you're all doing the reading.
Speaker 1: That's right. And as well as that, because of that, really, you can do, you know, much deeper research. So I thought we could try to revise what we've done on the geology course, because I know this is the one that most of us are worried about, the geology exam.
Speaker 2: Right. Yes. So the idea is we all look at a different topic, a different topic from the geology course, and then give a presentation and talk about it?
Speaker 1: That's right. I've drawn up the framework of a table which might be useful. Here. I've made a copy.
Speaker 3: Oh, thanks. For
Speaker 1: the first topic, I thought we could maybe do mountain building. Is that alright?
Speaker 2: Yeah. Sure. Actually, would you mind if I did that? I'm quite interested in it.
Speaker 1: Right.
Speaker 2: Right.
Speaker 1: So is May 9 okay for that?
Speaker 2: Mhmm. Yeah.
Speaker 1: I'll just write that down, and it's Bob for mountain building. And the following week, it can't be May 16 because of our tutorial. But what about the seventeenth?
Speaker 2: Okay. And what about the next topic? What would be the next priority?
Speaker 3: Well, there's glaciated areas, but I don't want to do that.
Speaker 1: Fair enough. Actually, I don't mind having a bash. I did an assignment on them. Glaciated areas, Andy. Then we need someone to do rock formation. Helen?
Speaker 3: Yeah. Okay. And John said he'd like to too, so you can put us both down for that.
Speaker 1: When?
Speaker 3: May 23 would be best.
Speaker 1: Rock formation, Helen and John. Right. That really only leaves one week before the exams. Shall we make it on the thirtieth?
Speaker 2: I can't make it, I'm afraid.
Speaker 1: May 29? The exam's on June 3.
Speaker 2: Have to be.
Speaker 1: Okay. Any ideas for a topic?
Speaker 2: John said he wouldn't mind doing something on volcanoes.
Speaker 1: Great. That's everyone then.
Speaker 0: Before you hear the rest of the conversation, you have some time to look at questions 26 to 30 on page seven. Now listen and answer questions 26 to 30.
Speaker 2: And how long should these presentations be?
Speaker 1: Well, it's obviously up to us. In my experience, thirty minutes is about enough.
Speaker 3: Maybe a bit short. I'd have thought forty minutes would be more like it.
Speaker 1: Well, should we say thirty to forty minutes? Okay. Uh-huh.
Speaker 2: And presumably time for questions.
Speaker 3: And discussion.
Speaker 1: Yes. Together they usually take about twenty minutes.
Speaker 3: Where should we get the information from? Is it mainly lecture notes?
Speaker 1: Well, actually, I suggest we avoid those because we already have all that information. I think it's better to go more deeply.
Speaker 2: We could use the bibliography.
Speaker 1: And anything else we find in the library, any other books.
Speaker 3: And articles, you know, from the journals.
Speaker 2: And then of course there's lots of stuff on the Internet.
Speaker 1: Yes, that's the sort of thing.
Speaker 2: And what about the presentations? Will we just be talking? Presumably, we we can't use slides.
Speaker 1: It'd be a bit difficult, but we can use the OHP.
Speaker 3: And the whiteboard, of course.
Speaker 2: And we can make photocopies of our notes so everyone can have a copy.
Speaker 1: Yes. Great. So is there anything else?
Speaker 0: That is the end of section three. You now have half a minute to check your answers. Now turn to section four on page eight.
